extracted.intended_audience: International Searching Authorities (ISA), International Preliminary Examining Authorities (IPEA), patent examiners, and applicants/agents preparing or responding to PCT written opinions and international preliminary examination reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required content for written opinions and international preliminary examination reports under the PCT, describing what examiners must include and how particular items (citations, priority, amendments, sequence listings, etc.) are to be treated and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of an article published in a periodical or other serial publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification should be made according to WIPO Standard ST.14 by the inclusion of the following:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) the name of the author (in capital letters). In case of multiple authors, preferably all names should be entered, alternatively the name of the first author followed by “et al.”; (ii) the title of the article (where appropriate, abbreviated or truncated); (iii) the title of the periodical or other serial publication (abbreviations conforming to generally recognized international practice may be used); (iv) the location within the periodical by indicating date of issue by four digits for the year, issue designation, pagination of the article (where year, month and day are available, apply WIPO Standard ST.2); (v) if available, the standard identifier (ISBN, ISSN) noting these may differ for printed and electronic versions; (vi) where applicable, the relevant passages of the article and/or relevant figures of the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of non-patent literature in a non-English language
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-patent literature citations in a language other than English, include the original (non-English) reference where technically possible, followed by an official translation into English, if one exists and is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an official translation into English is not available for some elements, an informal translation may optionally be provided after all elements of any official translation. Any informal translation should be preceded by the text “non-official translation”. "Official translation" means a rendering from the same source as the citation useful for identifying and retrieving the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of oral disclosures, use, exhibitions or other non-written public disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification should be made according to WIPO Standard ST.14, indicating the earliest date of the disclosure to the public, applying WIPO Standard ST.2 where year, month and day are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This could be the date of a public oral presentation, use or exhibition, or, for a private video recording, the date the recording was posted on the Internet. Later dates (e.g., date of publication of conference proceedings or posting of a public event) and the date of retrieval for an Internet citation should also be included. For audio/video, indicate specific timeline sections (e.g., “from 01:22 to 01:56”). See paragraph 11.22 for internet posting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing a document that refers to an earlier oral disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents refer to an earlier oral disclosure, use, exhibition or other means (e.g., conference proceedings or Internet posting), provide details of the earlier disclosure first, followed by the document that refers to the prior disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO Standard ST.14 contains examples of how to cite such chains of disclosure (example formats shown in the guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of relevance for citations in supplementary international search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: In supplementary international search reports, an explanation may be included regarding why the citation is considered relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists readers (especially where citations are in languages not well understood by the applicant or Offices). If the explanation can be made in a few words without making the list difficult to read, include it with the main citation; if longer explanation is needed, add a separate sheet for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating relevant claims for 'A' citations
rubrics_metrics.description: For “A” citations it is not necessary to indicate the relevant claims unless there is good reason to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of good reason include a clear lack of unity a priori where the citation is relevant only to a particular claim or group of claims, or when the claims meet criteria of novelty, inventive step, and industrial applicability and the A-category citations represent the most relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing patent family members in the patent family annex
rubrics_metrics.description: Known family members of each cited citation are normally listed in the patent family annex of the international search report to enable readers worldwide to consider citations in the most convenient document/language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If INPADOC is used note the limitations: (a) INPADOC does not provide family listings for documents published prior to 1968; (b) If INPADOC indicates no family members, enter the word “NONE” where family members would appear to indicate a family search was carried out; (c) If INPADOC indicates none of the citations has a family member, still check the “See patent family annex” box and follow paragraph (b) for all citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent family annex to indicate corresponding English passages
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent family annex may be used to indicate the corresponding part or passage of the English member of a patent family if the cited patent document is in a language other than English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 15.69 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Authority and report drafting and mailing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The identification of the International Searching Authority which established the international search report and the date on which the report was drawn up are indicated at the bottom of the second sheet of the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The drafting date should be that of the drafting of the report by the examiner who carried out the search. The international search report also indicates the date on which it was mailed to the applicant, which is important for computing time limits for filing amendments under Article 19.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner name and date of actual completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is an authorized officer his name will appear on the search report; where not an authorized officer the name of the responsible examiner supervising the report should be entered as the authorized officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the examiner is an authorized officer the date of actual completion will be entered by that officer; where not authorized the “date of completion” should be entered after the responsible officer has supervised the report and any corrections have been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and provision of copies of references cited
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority should preferably attach copies of all references cited to the copy of the international search report sent to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation of such copies may require a separate request and payment of a separate fee. Copies may be sent to any designated Office or the applicant upon request any time during seven years from the international filing date. Forms PCT/ISA/221 (invitation for payment of fees) and PCT/ISA/211 (request for copies) may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of a written opinion is to give a primary indication to the applicant of the defects which the examiner considers to exist so the applicant can determine the most appropriate course of action (demand IPE, submit comments/amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its primary role is to identify whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, involve an inventive step (be non-obvious) and be industrially applicable. It will also include opinions on certain other substantive defects insofar as checked by the Authority and on certain form defects of the international application (see Rules referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship of ISA written opinion to IPEA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A written opinion will be issued by the International Searching Authority together with the international search report and will normally be treated as the first written opinion of the International Preliminary Examining Authority under Article 34(2) if international preliminary examination is demanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment usually includes an invitation to submit a response with a time-limit. IPEAs may notify the International Bureau if they will not treat certain ISA written opinions as their first written opinion; such notifications are published in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters a written opinion should cover (Rule 66.2 matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any written opinion should usually cover matters such as (i) whether Article 34(4) situations apply; (ii) an apparent failure to meet novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability; (iii) defects in form or contents insofar as checked; (iv) amendments appearing to go beyond the disclosure; (v) apparent lack of clarity or support for claims; (vi) that a claim is directed to an invention on which no international search report has been established; (vii) nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the principal substantive headings examiners should address in written opinions and international preliminary examination reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form/parts of the written opinion or international preliminary examination report
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from the cover sheet, these follow the same format and include (as appropriate): (i) Basis of the opinion or report; (ii) Priority; (iii) Non-establishment of opinion re novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability; (iv) Lack of unity of invention; (v) Reasoned statement with citations; (vi) Certain documents cited; (vii) Certain defects in the international application; (viii) Certain observations on the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blank sheets which have not been filled in are to be omitted and not included in total sheet count on the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet data to be included
rubrics_metrics.description: The following data (insofar as set out on the cover sheet) are to be included: (i) international application number; (ii) name of the applicant; (iii) name of the International Authority; (iv) international filing date; (v) classification (at least IPC); (vi) claimed priority date; (vii) applicant’s or agent’s file reference (≤25 characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items appear on the cover sheet per Rules 43bis.1(b), 70.3-70.5 and must be present where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification statement in report
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of the classification repeats the classification given by the International Searching Authority if the examiner agrees with such classification, or, if not, sets forth the classification the examiner considers correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 7 for classification handling and Rule 43.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the opinion/report (application version)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion of the ISA is established on the basis of the application as filed (or a translation) and, where rectifications or amendments have occurred, the opinion should take these into account and indicate the relevant replacement sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of “originally filed sheets” appear in paragraphs 17.16 and 17.16A; replacement/rectified sheets should be identified as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language indication for elements of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: If elements of the application were not available or furnished in the language in which the international application was filed, an appropriate indication must be checked as to whether elements were furnished in (i) the language of a translation furnished for the purposes of international search, (ii) the language of publication, or (iii) the language of the translation furnished for international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Rules 23.1(b), 48.3(b), 55.2 and 55.3 and refer to Chapter 18 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheets deemed part of the application as originally filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement pages or sheets filed in response to an invitation by the receiving Office to correct defects and rectifications of obvious errors under Rule 91 are deemed to be part of the international application 'as originally filed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such sheets should be identified (e.g., “SUBSTITUTE SHEET (RULE 26)”, “RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91)”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheets incorporated after filing date or marked 'INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE'
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets submitted after the date when Article 11(1) requirements were fulfilled and accepted by the receiving Office after a change of international filing date, or sheets accepted under Rule 20.6(b) and marked 'INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE (Rule 20.6)', are also deemed part of the application as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such sheets are notified to the ISA after it has begun the search it may invite applicant to pay additional fees to consider them for international search; if additional fees are not paid the written opinion will be based on the application without those sheets and this is noted in item 5 'Additional comments' of Box No. I.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERRONEOUSLY FILED sheets handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets stamped 'ERRONEOUSLY FILED (RULE 20.5bis)' usually need not be taken into account for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist as described (see paragraph 15.11) and context should be checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication when opinion/report is based on amended international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a written opinion or report is based on the international application as originally filed or furnished, this is noted by checking the appropriate box; where amendments have been filed the report indicates the version of each page on which the opinion or report is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures clarity about which document version the opinion addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments under Article 19 identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments under Article 19 have been made by the applicant they should be referred to in Box No. I, item 2 as 'claims: Nos. ... as amended under Article 19'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Article 19 only claims may be amended; such sheets are usually identified 'AMENDED SHEET (ARTICLE 19)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments under Article 34 identification and dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments under Article 34 have been made they should be referred to as 'claims: Nos. ... received by this Authority on ...' and the amendments should indicate the dates as the 'received on' dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superseded amendments are not normally included except in cases where a later replacement sheet goes beyond original disclosure (see handling of superseded replacement sheets). See Rule 70.16 and Section 602.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of superseded replacement sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: If a first replacement sheet is acceptable and a second replacement sheet for the same numbered sheet contains subject matter that goes beyond the original disclosure, the second replacement sheet supersedes the first replacement sheet, but both the first and second replacement sheets are attached to the international preliminary examination report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superseded replacement sheets are marked 'SUPERSEDED REPLACEMENT SHEET (RULE 70.16(b))' in addition to other marks indicating when received as amendment sheets. When Annexes contain final amendments that go beyond original disclosure and earlier amendments that form part of the basis of the report, this is noted in the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings used for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more of the following indications must be given with respect to the sequence listing on which the examination is based: (a) forming part of the international application as filed; (b) furnished subsequent to the international filing date for purposes of international search/prelim exam (also indicating whether accompanied by a statement that listing does not go beyond disclosure); (c) furnished as an amendment under Article 34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a required sequence listing was not furnished in accepted form, the written opinion/report must indicate whether a meaningful opinion could be formed without such listing (see Chapter 18 for further details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicating amendments resulting in gaps in numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments under Article 19 or 34 have been made which result in cancellation or gaps in numbering sequence of description pages, claim numbers, and/or drawing sheets, these are detailed in item 3 of Box No. I of the written opinion/report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records structural changes to the application numbering caused by amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and reporting of amendments going beyond the original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments have been made which go beyond the original disclosure of the application as filed, the examiner identifies said amended sheet(s) in item 4 of Box No. I and gives brief reasons in a Supplemental Box sheet; these amendments are attached to the report as Annexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 17.20 for related handling of superseded replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-up searches reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a top-up search has been carried out by the International Preliminary Examining Authority, the appropriate indication must be given in item 6 of Box No. I of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a top-up search has been carried out, the examiner also indicates the date of the top-up search and whether additional relevant documents were discovered during that search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of amendments not accompanied by a letter indicating their basis in the application as filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments have been made but the replacement sheet(s) was not accompanied by a letter indicating the basis for the amendment in the application as filed and the report is established as if the amendment had not been made, the examiner identifies said amended sheet(s) in item 4 of Box No. I and attaches these amendments as Annexes in addition to any amended sheets which form part of the basis of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also paragraph 17.20 regarding superseded sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rectification of an obvious mistake is taken into account under Rule 66.1, the report shall indicate this in item 5 of Box No. I; if not taken into account pursuant to Rule 66.4bis the report shall, if possible, so indicate, failing which the IPEA shall notify the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records whether rectifications of obvious mistakes were considered in preparing the opinion/report and ensures appropriate notification where not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority box relevance and checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. II (Priority) is not relevant if the international application does not claim priority. Where priority is claimed but all citations were published before the earliest priority date, it is not necessary to consider whether the priority claim is valid and this Box should normally not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where one or more citations were published after the earliest priority date, validity of the earliest priority date requires checking. If the priority document is in the Authority's records, obtain it; if not available before preparation of the written opinion the ISA may establish the written opinion as if the priority had been validly claimed and note this in Box No. II item 1. If the priority document is provided later, the IPEA and/or report should reconsider the validity of the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures if priority document is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of the priority document (or necessary translation) is not available before preparing the written opinion and it is not in records or available from a digital library, the written opinion may be established as if the priority had been validly claimed and this fact noted; alternatively, if not available because of non-compliance by the applicant within the relevant time period, the written opinion/report may be established as if the priority had not been claimed and this indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate comments should be made under 'Additional observations' in Box No. II. If the right to priority is invalid, item 2 of Box No. II must be completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional observations in Box No. II limited to priority considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional observations in item 3 of Box No. II relate only to priority considerations and not to clarity, descriptive support, defects or any other consideration relevant to Box No. VIII.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such observations might include reasons why a priority claim was considered invalid or an indication that it had been checked and considered valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-establishment of opinion with regard to novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability (Box No. III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. III explains why an opinion as regards novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability may not have been established for some or all of the subject matter (e.g., excluded subject matter, lack of clarity/support, or no international search made).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first two check boxes indicate extent of non-establishment; reasons may be identical to reasons in the international search report (reference allowed). Provide observations on lack of clarity/support to explain limitation of examination where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter excluded under Rule 67.1
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some or all claims are not examined for novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability because they contain excluded subject matter, this observation is indicated in the third check box of Box No. III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 43bis.1(b) and 67.1 (and agreements with the International Bureau) explain categories excluded from examination (e.g., certain mathematical methods, plant/animal varieties, methods of treatment) and qualifying exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity or support issues causing non-establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description, claims, or drawings are so unclear, or the claims are so inadequately supported by the description that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability, the examination may be restricted to claims/parts sufficiently clear and supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an opinion cannot be established on a claim the examiner marks the appropriate check box in Box No. III and includes observations on lack of clarity and/or support. Issues of clarity and descriptive support should be raised separately from novelty/inventive step considerations in Box No. VIII (see Chapter 5 and paragraph 17.50).

rubrics_metrics.name: No international search made for some or all claims (Article 33(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISA has not established an international search report and instead issued a declaration under Article 17 (relating to excluded subject matter, clarity, lack of unity, etc.), the questions of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability cannot be addressed and this is noted using the sixth check box of Box No. III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even where Article 34 amendments may have overcome earlier considerations. See Article 33(6).
